title: Why a static block cannot replace a constructor
answer: A static block and a constructor have different lifecycles. The static block runs once per class initialization and can initialize class-level state; a constructor runs for every new object and initializes instance state. Therefore a static block cannot replace constructors when each object needs its own validated fields. A class can use both, but they solve different problems.
